symptoms: Small circular to angular, dark-brown or black sunken necrotic spots on leaves, petioles, and stems. Lesions on pods are circular and depressed with raised reddish-brown margins. Premature leaf drop and pod discoloration occur in severe infections.
management_method: Integrated Pest Management (Cultural, Biological, Chemical). Use certified disease-free seeds. Crop rotation for 2-3 seasons with non-legume crops. Deep summer ploughing to bury crop residues. Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride @ 4 g/kg seed or Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10 g/kg seed.
recommended_pesticide_or_treatment: Seed treatment: Carbendazim 50% WP @ 2.0 g/kg seed or Thiram 75% WP @ 2.0 g/kg seed. Foliar spray at first appearance of lesions: Carbendazim 50% WP @ 1.0 g/L (500 g/ha in 500 L water) OR Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.0 g/L (1000 g/ha) OR Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC @ 1.0 ml/L. Repeat at 10-14 day intervals if humid rainy weather persists. Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI): 15-20 days.
fertilizer_or_nutrient_advice: Fertilizer is for crop nutrition and growth, NOT a cure for fungal infection. Recommended basal application: 20 kg N, 40 kg P2O5, 20 kg K2O, and 20 kg Sulfur per hectare. Foliar spray of 2% DAP (20 g/L) or 1% Potassium Chloride (MOP) at flower initiation and 15 days later to enhance crop recovery, root nodule activity, and pod set.
source: ICAR-IIPR (Indian Institute of Pulses Research) Package of Practices, ICAR-NCIPM IPM Package for Urdbean, and TNAU Agritech Portal (Crop Protection: Pulses).
precautions: Do not apply chemical fungicides during strong winds (>15 km/h) or hot midday sun. Observe the 15-20 day Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI) before picking pods. Wear PPE (gloves, mask). If uncertain of pathogen or if disease affects >30% of field, consult an agricultural expert.

symptoms: Leaves exhibit uniform deep green coloration, active photosynthetic chlorophyll, intact trifoliate architecture, and complete absence of necrotic lesions, chlorosis, crinkling, or viral mosaic patterns.
management_method: Preventative Cultural & Scouting Management. Inspect fields every 7 days. Maintain proper drainage to prevent waterlogging and root rot. Keep field weed-free during the critical first 30 days after sowing.
recommended_pesticide_or_treatment: No chemical pesticide application required. Prophylactic chemical spraying is strictly discouraged to protect natural predatory insects (ladybird beetles, hoverflies, Chrysoperla) and honeybees. Preventative biological spray: Neem oil (Azadirachtin 0.03% / 300 PPM) @ 3-5 ml/L if sucking pest counts begin to rise.
fertilizer_or_nutrient_advice: Maintain balanced biological nitrogen fixation. Recommended basal dose: 20 kg N, 40 kg P2O5, 20 kg K2O per hectare. Seed inoculation with Rhizobium culture @ 600 g/ha + Phosphobacteria (PSB) @ 600 g/ha before sowing. Foliar micronutrient spray: 0.5% Zinc Sulfate + 0.2% Borax at 25-30 days after sowing if native soil is deficient.
source: TNAU Agritech Portal (Pulses: Blackgram Agronomy) and ICAR-IIPR Pulse Production Guidelines.
precautions: Avoid excessive nitrogenous top-dressing as excess nitrogen hampers root nodulation and increases susceptibility to sap-sucking pests.

symptoms: Severe crinkling, rugosity, puckering, and thickening of leaves, starting from the third trifoliate leaf. Malformation of leaves into cup-shaped structures, stunted internodes, severe floral abnormality (phyllody - petals turning into leafy structures), and partial or complete sterility of flowers.
management_method: Integrated Vector & Sanitation Management. ULCV is a systemic virus; chemical fungicides CANNOT cure established viral infections. Rogue out (uproot) and bury/burn affected plants within 3 to 4 weeks of germination to eliminate field inoculum. Use certified disease-free seeds from healthy mother crops. Hot water seed treatment at 55°C for 30 minutes before sowing.
recommended_pesticide_or_treatment: Direct cure: No chemical cures viral infections. Vector control is mandatory to stop secondary spread. Seed treatment: Imidacloprid 70% WS @ 5.0 g/kg seed or Thiamethoxam 30% FS @ 5.0 ml/kg seed for 25-day vector protection. Vector control foliar spray: Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.3 ml/L (100-125 ml/ha in 500 L water) OR Thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 0.25 g/L (100 g/ha) OR Dimethoate 30% EC @ 1.7 ml/L at first observation of aphid or whitefly colonies. Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI): 15-21 days.
fertilizer_or_nutrient_advice: Fertilizers cannot cure viral infections. Do not apply fertilizer as a remedy for disease. For non-infected surrounding plants: Foliar spray of Potassium Nitrate (13-0-45) @ 10 g/L (1%) or Pulse Wonder @ 2 kg/acre at peak flowering to boost systemic plant vigor and stress tolerance.
source: ICAR-NCIPM (Urdbean Integrated Pest Management Guidelines) and TNAU Agritech Portal (Blackgram Diseases).
precautions: Do not spray insecticides during peak honeybee pollination hours. Rogue infected plants before spraying so vectors do not scatter virus to neighboring plants. For severe viral spread across >30% crop, consult an agricultural expert immediately.

symptoms: Small, faint, white circular powdery patches appear on the upper surface of older leaves, rapidly expanding and covering both leaf surfaces, petioles, stems, and developing pods. Leaves turn dull yellow, chlorotic, curl upwards, and drop prematurely. Late infection causes small, shriveled, unmarketable seeds.
management_method: Cultural, Biological, and Chemical IPM. Sowing in late June or early July helps the crop escape late-season cool/dry infection periods. Collect and burn crop residue after harvest. Avoid excessively dense plant populations (maintain 30 x 10 cm spacing). Bio-control: Foliar spray of Ampelomyces quisqualis @ 5 g/L or 1% baking soda (sodium bicarbonate) as an organic deterrent.
recommended_pesticide_or_treatment: Foliar spray at first sign of white powdery spots: Wettable Sulfur 80% WP @ 2.5-3.0 g/L (1.25-1.5 kg/ha in 500 L water) OR Hexaconazole 5% EC @ 1.0 ml/L (500 ml/ha) OR Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1.0 ml/L OR Dinocap 48% EC @ 1.0 ml/L. Repeat after 10-14 days if cool night temperatures (15-20°C) and cloudy/dry days persist. Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI): 15-20 days.
fertilizer_or_nutrient_advice: Fertilizer is for crop nutrition, NOT a cure for powdery mildew. Fertilizers do not cure powdery mildew and cannot eliminate fungal infection. Excessive nitrogen worsens infection. Avoid excess urea/nitrogen top-dressing as tender succulent growth promotes rapid fungal colonization. Apply adequate basal Potash (MOP @ 20-25 kg K2O/ha) to strengthen leaf cuticle thickness and natural disease resistance.
source: ICAR-IIPR Kanpur, TNAU Agritech Portal (Pulses Protection: Powdery Mildew), and CIBRC Major Uses of Pesticides (Pulses).
precautions: Do not spray sulfur formulations when the ambient temperature is higher than 35°C, as sulfur can cause severe phytotoxic leaf scorch. Always observe safety waiting periods before harvesting. If disease persists, consult an agricultural expert.

symptoms: Yellow mosaic pattern appearing as small chlorotic yellow specks along the leaf veins, gradually expanding and coalescing into large bright golden-yellow patches interspersed with green areas. In severe cases, the entire foliage turns completely yellow or bleached white. Leaves become small and brittle; pods are severely stunted, deformed, and produce few or shriveled grains.
management_method: Integrated Vector & Genetic Resistance Strategy. Viral pathogens have NO curative chemical treatments. Grow resistant varieties certified by ICAR/TNAU: VBN 4, VBN 6, VBN 8, LBG 752, Mash 114, Uttara, PU 31. Install yellow sticky traps @ 15-20 traps/acre at canopy level to monitor and mass-trap adult whiteflies. Rogue out and destroy diseased plants within 20 days of germination.
recommended_pesticide_or_treatment: Direct cure: Not curable chemically. Do NOT spray fungicides. Seed treatment: Imidacloprid 70% WS @ 5.0 g/kg seed or Thiamethoxam 30% FS @ 5.0 ml/kg seed (protects plants from whiteflies for 20-25 days). Whitefly vector spray: Diafenthiuron 50% WP @ 1.0 g/L (500 g/ha in 500 L water) OR Acetamiprid 20% SP @ 0.2 g/L (100 g/ha) OR Thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 0.25 g/L (100 g/ha). Direct spray to the undersides of leaves where whiteflies colonize. Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI): 15-21 days.
fertilizer_or_nutrient_advice: Fertilizer is NOT a cure for Yellow Mosaic Virus. It supports general nutritional balance. Foliar Spray: 2% DAP (20 g/L) + 1% Potassium Chloride (MOP, 10 g/L) or TNAU Pulse Wonder @ 2 kg/acre at 30 and 45 days after sowing to minimize yield loss in non-severely affected plants and promote pod development.
source: ICAR-NCIPM (Urdbean IPM Package), TNAU Agritech Portal (Plant Pathology: Pulses), and ICAR-IIPR MYMV Advisory Bulletin.
precautions: Rotate insecticide classes (e.g., neonicotinoids and thioureas) to prevent insecticide resistance in Bemisia tabaci. Do not spray during wind or heavy rainfall. If infection exceeds 50% of field in early vegetative stage, consult an agricultural expert immediately.
